about: What real use, and the person Pit Board is for, showed must change or must stay true in Windstorm Pit Board, and the version each is due in. A lesson here is a gate, not a note: tests/test_g21_promises.py (G21.14) refuses a version while a row due in it is not built, and refuses the version after it until the row says where it was proven on a real machine.
how_to_use: A new lesson gets a row the day it is learned: what was seen, the promise, a codon in DNA-STRAND-MASTER-PLAN.md, the version it is due in, and a tracking issue when work is left.
When it is built: put the name of its test in 'test'. The test must exist under tests/ and be named with the row's codon (test_G10_5_... for G10.5).
When it has been seen to work on a real machine: say which machine, which version and when in 'proven'.

'ship_in' moves only with a reason in 'moved_why'. A row whose owner is 'person' was seen by the person Pit Board is for, on their own machine: its date moves only by their word, restated in 'moved_by_person'.
A row is never deleted. A promise that turns out wrong is closed by a row that says why.
A lesson that was heard and not taken goes under 'declined' with the reason, so that nothing is dropped without a word.

VT, FF and the C0 separators come through, because the writer escapes them. Right after add, the board still shows the ask, because add folds its own event into the state cache and the board reads that cache while it matches the log's size. Every road that folds the log loses it from the first moment: board --all, list --all, show, export. The board, status and reminder show it only until the state is next rebuilt. The roads that rebuild it in real use, as read in the code: (i) any act on an ID the cache does not hold live (an answer, ok, no, done, withdraw or update on a closed ask, a mistyped ID or the lost ask's own ID: the command retries with every ask and writes the state from a whole fold); (ii) every reopen; (iii) a write whose event sorts before the lane's newest, or names an ask the cache does not hold; (iv) uninstall, which removes the state and keeps the logs; (v) a cache that is missing, unreadable, or left behind by a writer stopped after its lines; (vi) a reader that finds the lane busy folds without writing, for that one read. An update from 0.1.2 is not one of them. After that rebuild, the next add gives out the lost ask's number again, so one log holds two different asks under one ID. An answer whose words hold one of those characters is lost the same way: answer said "A1 answered.", show said open, and after a rebuild the board counted it open again. The first sighting was on a road that folds the log. With only the reader cured, a cache an older copy wrote still matches the log's size and keeps the lost ask off the board, and answer, ok and done on a doubled ID each act on one of the two asks without saying so, the one the cache happens to hold.
